vectors.name: depth-32-arrays
vectors.why: B1: 32 nested arrays, the innermost empty, decode under the default depth bound, 32 (CD-B1)

vectors.name: depth-33-arrays
vectors.why: B2: a 33rd nested array is one beyond the default bound: TooDeep, though it is empty

vectors.name: depth-32-maps
vectors.why: B3: 32 nested maps, each holding the next under key 0, decode: a map counts as an array does

vectors.name: depth-33-maps
vectors.why: B4: a 33rd nested map is TooDeep

vectors.name: depth-32-scalar-leaf
vectors.why: B5: an int inside the 32nd array adds no depth: ints, strings, bools, null and floats never count

vectors.name: depth-33-items-missing
vectors.why: B6: the 33rd array's head is complete and its item missing: depth is checked once a head is read, before its first item, so TooDeep and not Truncated (CD-B2)

vectors.name: depth-33-torn-head
vectors.why: B7: the 33rd array's head claims an 8-byte count and holds one byte: a torn head is Truncated, before depth is checked (CD-B2)

vectors.name: depth-33-mixed
vectors.why: B8: arrays and maps alternating, 33 deep: both count toward the one bound

vectors.name: depth-100000-arrays
vectors.why: B9: 100,000 nested arrays are refused at the 33rd, with no stack overflow, RecursionError or RangeError on the way (CD-E4)

vectors.name: depth-100000-maps
vectors.why: B10: 100,000 nested maps, as B9

vectors.name: depth-33-unknown-field
vectors.why: B11: an IntBox whose unknown field 9 holds 32 nested arrays, 33 deep with the message's map: depth counts unknown fields, and the raw stage refuses them before the schema stage runs (CD-B2)

vectors.name: depth-32-unknown-field
vectors.why: B12: the same with 31 arrays, 32 deep, decodes: a codec that keeps unknown fields writes field 9 back, one that drops them writes the IntBox alone

vectors.name: size-at-limit
vectors.why: B13: four bytes under a raw call's max_encoded_len of 4 decode: input exactly at the bound is accepted (CD-B5)

vectors.name: size-over-limit
vectors.why: B14: the same four bytes under a bound of 3 are TooLarge, naming the input's length and the bound (CD-B4)

vectors.name: size-before-parse
vectors.why: B15: the length is checked before a byte is read: four CBOR tags, UnsupportedMajor once read, are TooLarge under a bound of 3 (CD-E5 step 1)

vectors.name: size-empty
vectors.why: B16: empty input is within a bound of 0, so it is read, and is Truncated (CD-B5)

vectors.name: depth-64-declared
vectors.why: B17: a Tree64 64 deep decodes: a typed decode applies its root's declared max_depth, 64 (CD-B3)

vectors.name: depth-65-declared
vectors.why: B18: a Tree64 65 deep is TooDeep{64}

vectors.name: raw-ignores-declared
vectors.why: B19: B17's bytes through the raw decode, which knows no schema, meet the default bound (CD-B3)

vectors.name: depth-root-decides
vectors.why: B20: a Tree64 inside a Holds64, 33 deep: the root, Holds64, declares nothing, so 32 bounds the whole call though Tree64 declares 64 (OPT-D4)

vectors.name: depth-2-declared
vectors.why: B21: a Flat2 at its declared bound, 2, its own non-recursive nesting, decodes

vectors.name: depth-3-declared
vectors.why: B22: an array inside Flat2's list is 3 deep: TooDeep{2} from the raw stage, before the schema stage would find a WrongType (CD-E5)

vectors.name: depth-128-ceiling
vectors.why: B23: a Tree128 128 deep, at the ceiling, decodes (CD-B5)

vectors.name: depth-129-ceiling
vectors.why: B24: a Tree128 129 deep is TooDeep{128}

vectors.name: raw-depth-128
vectors.why: B25: a raw call passing max_depth 128 decodes 128 nested arrays

vectors.name: raw-depth-129
vectors.why: B26: the same call refuses 129

vectors.name: raw-depth-capped
vectors.why: B27: a raw call passing max_depth 1000 applies the ceiling, and TooDeep names the bound applied, 128 (CD-B3, question 1)

vectors.name: len-8-declared
vectors.why: B28: a Sized8 of exactly 8 bytes decodes under its declared max_encoded_len, 8

vectors.name: len-9-declared
vectors.why: B29: a Sized8 of 9 bytes is TooLarge, before a byte is read (CD-B4)

vectors.name: len-root-decides
vectors.why: B30: a Sized8 longer than 8 bytes inside a HoldsSized8 decodes: the root declares no length bound, and Sized8's does not apply inside it (OPT-D4)
